oneliner.t: Republican from Haleyville who has represented north-central Alabama's 4th District since 1997, dean of the state's House delegation and chairman of the Appropriations subcommittee on Labor, Health and Human Services and Education; he won the May 19, 2026 GOP primary and faces Democrat Amanda Pusczek.

upbringing.t: Aderholt is the only child of Mary Frances Brown and Bobby Ray Aderholt, who served as an Alabama circuit judge for about 30 years and was a part-time minister. He graduated from Haleyville High School in 1979, attended the University of North Alabama, and earned a B.A. in history and political science from Birmingham-Southern College (1987) and a J.D. from Samford's Cumberland School of Law (1990). He practiced law, was appointed Haleyville municipal judge in 1992, and became a legal aide to Gov. Fob James in 1995 before winning the open 4th District seat in 1996. He married Caroline McDonald, daughter of former state senator and Agriculture Commissioner Albert McDonald, in 1994; they have two children.

platform.t: Lists economic development, job creation, strong immigration policy and national security as priorities; touts constituent casework.
Chairs the Values Action Team, a member group focused on families, communities and religious freedom; introduced the Ten Commandments Defense Act (1998, 2002, 2003).
Co-sponsored the Birthright Citizenship Act and introduced a bill to make English the official language.
Introduced a 2019 bill to raise the minimum tobacco purchase age to 21.

note.t: Latest annual report opened is for calendar 2023 (signed Aug. 13, 2024, under extension). Largest holdings: an Arlington, VA home (joint, $1M–$5M); his spouse's 21% stake in Greenbrier Enterprises LLC ($1M–$5M); Hoggle Ridge Properties LLC ($1M–$5M, mortgage $500K–$1M); Armadale Properties LLC (spouse, $500K–$1M); whole-life insurance ($500K–$1M); and Alabama municipal bonds. Small stock positions include foreign ADRs (America Movil, Banco Santander, GSK, Haleon) and Navistar. Liabilities: Arlington mortgage $250K–$500K; Hoggle Ridge mortgage $500K–$1M. 2023 transactions were bond sales and the health-fund/Haleon exchanges; a Sept. 2025 PTR reports a GSK sale (July 28, 2025). The net-worth range is assets minus liabilities from the disclosure ranges, includes the Arlington home, and excludes one 'undetermined' money-market fund. Reported travel: Fellowship Foundation-paid trip to Serbia and Croatia, May 25–30, 2023. The trades are small; no link between them and any official act is documented.

democracy.t: Signed the December 2020 House Republican amicus brief supporting Texas v. Pennsylvania (one of 126); the Supreme Court declined the case.

During the Jan. 6 attack tweeted a prayer for God to 'guide & protect this nation'; later said some attackers 'crossed the line.'
